edges.notes: Ubuntu ships Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
Ubuntu is a Debian-derived distribution: dpkg/apt packaging lineage and archive heritage with Canonical governance and distinct release cadence.
Ubuntu desktop and server on standard ports use glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd is the default init and service manager on current Ubuntu LTS and interim releases per Ubuntu documentation themes.
Ubuntu services are expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs.
Ubuntu userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages are central to Ubuntu build-essential and package build flows.
GNU binutils participate in standard Ubuntu package build and link flows.
g++-built packages link GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical Ubuntu GNU/Linux flows.
Clang/LLVM packages are available from Ubuntu archives for alternative compiler stacks.
Official ubuntu and ubuntu:* OCI images are common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
CRI/containerd nodes run Ubuntu-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts.
Kubernetes nodes and pods frequently use Ubuntu-class images on Linux; not exclusive.
Ubuntu bases are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
